# EvSeparator

> A separator is a thin line that visually divides content into groups — between list items, sections, or side-by-side elements — without adding emphasis.

| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |

| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-separator">` |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Separator**, frame `4045:62753` (Separator). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to divide groups of related content (list rows, menu sections, form blocks).
- Use a vertical separator between inline items in a toolbar or stat row.
- Use to set a card or panel header/footer apart from its body.
- Use sparingly — reach for spacing first, lines second.

### When not to use

- Don't use just to decorate  →  use spacing
- Don't stack lines for emphasis  →  use a heading
- Don't put a line around every item  →  group with whitespace
- Don't use as a container border  →  use a Card (`evoq-ui:card`) / stroke

### Do

- Keep the line thin and low-contrast (1px, neutral)
- Align separators to the content edges
- Prefer whitespace; add a line only when grouping is unclear
- Match the length to the content it divides

### Don't

- Use heavy or colored lines for plain division
- Indent separators inconsistently in a list
- Separate every single row in a dense list
- Use a line where a gap would read better

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvSeparator`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-separator">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:separator` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
